title: Nanoelectromechanical Binary Comparator for Edge-Computing Applications
problem: Binary comparison is fundamental in arithmetic and ML algorithms but CMOS implementations waste power on standby; harsh edge environments (high temperature, radiation) require robust comparators.
motivation: Edge computing in industrial settings demands power efficiency and reliability under extreme conditions; nanoelectromechanical devices offer inherent robustness and zero standby power.
method: Implements binary comparators using 4-terminal nanoelectromechanical (NEM) relays: single 1-bit magnitude and equality comparators use only 6 devices vs 9 transistors in CMOS. Fabricated on silicon-on-insulator substrate. Scalable tree-based topology for higher-order comparators achieves ~47% device reduction vs CMOS for 64-bit comparators.
key_novelty: First silicon-fabricated NEM relay comparators demonstrating higher integration density, extreme temperature tolerance (300°C), radiation hardness (>1 Mrad), and zero standby power.
contributions: 6 devices per bit vs 9 CMOS transistors
21 fJ energy per operation (9x reduction vs best CMOS)
First silicon proof-of-concept with electrical characterization
limitations: Limited to 1-bit demonstration; scalability to complex arithmetic circuits and actual ML workloads not demonstrated; manufacturing yield not discussed.
primary_theme: NEM relay comparators for radiation-hard edge computing
